setting_and_object.category: Architecture / System (open-sourced vision-language interaction model plus deployable system)

details: Today's multimodal models and video-call products are structurally turn-based: they only respond when addressed or when an external polling trigger fires, so they cannot react to events in a live visual stream at the moment those events occur.
Needed instead: a model that continuously watches the present stream and decides for itself when speaking is worthwhile.

JoyAI-VL-Interaction: an ~8B vision-first 'interaction model' in which 'when to act' is a learned per-second decision internal to the model, emitting one of three actions each second over the streaming video: stay silent (a first-class action), respond, or delegate a hard subtask to an asynchronous background model.

Trained from time-aligned per-second action-labeled streaming data with a role-weighted token loss plus RL on stream-level timing rewards; speech (ASR/TTS) is deliberately kept outside the model as pluggable I/O so vision is the intrinsic proactive trigger.

Released alongside a complete deployable system: streaming ingestion, hierarchical long-horizon memory designed for prefix reuse on standard vLLM, and a background-agnostic delegation bridge to any API/model/agent.

Built on JoyAI-VL 1.0 (Qwen3-8B LM + Qwen3-VL ViT, projection trained from scratch; aligned, VL-pretrained, then on-policy distillation + RL) which is a conventional turn-based VLM before interaction training.

Video tokenized with AdaCodec predictive visual coding: full ViT tokens only at reference frames chosen by predictive-cost reset, ~16 tokens per predictable frame, so cost scales with scene change rather than frame count.
Streaming input sampled at 1 Hz by default; special control tokens </silence>, </response>, </delegation>.

Over 4M time-aligned streaming clips in six families: proactive alerting/anomaly detection, time-aligned QA (backward/present/forward timing), counting and perception over time, live commentary/narration, multi-turn casual chat, and cross-cutting delegation episodes (STEM, video-grounded knowledge, video reasoning).

Construction pipelines per family: larger VLM marks evidence onsets for QA timing; two VLM agents converse over a playing video with 3-frame anchoring for chat; ASR over real commentary footage for natural speech/silence cadence; temporal-grounding conversion plus dense 1fps precheck to ensure alerts mark a genuine first onset.

Delegation episodes scripted by a multi-role agent pipeline (Planner, Timestamp/Visual Verifier, Background agent, Foreground Rewriter), including a holding reply, hidden delegate query, and a randomized background latency so the model must stay present while a delegation is pending.
Every example passes global (whole-clip) and local (trigger-frame) verifier checks.
Single supervised continue-training stage mixing time-aligned interaction data into a large pool of conventional turn-based data.
Role-weighted cross-entropy on assistant tokens: repeated </silence> weighted 0.4, </response> weighted 1.5, first </silence> and other tokens 1; weighting applied only to time-aligned data.

GRPO RL stage with answer-centered window sampling (compressing hundreds of mostly-silent turns to a handful), rewards for correct and well-timed responses, appropriate silence, and well-judged delegation; penalties for false alarms, mistimed responses, always-respond degeneration; LLM-judge rubric scoring for content quality. Run on EasyVideoR1.
WebRTC/RTSP ingestion (aiortc, PyAV), OpenAI-compatible multimodal Chat Completions requests, stateful server-side sessions keyed by session_id.

Three-tier hierarchical memory (short-term raw vision tokens, mid-term textual summaries, long-term compressed blocks) plus dialogue memory, with asynchronous consolidation; text tiers form a stable per-chunk prefix that vLLM's prefix cache reuses, sustaining >2 hours of continuous video at sub-second end-to-end latency.

Pluggable open-source defaults: FunASR ASR, CosyVoice TTS, NVIDIA live-vlm-webui-derived UI, background bridge with task-id/query/note/frame-snapshot contract, fixed timeout, bounded digest returned into context.

Six event-driven live scenarios (monitoring/alerting, real-time counting, real-time translation, time awareness, live commentary/guidance, long-horizon memory), 58 cases total, mostly public web footage, replayed as an RTSP live stream via MediaMTX; memory config T_s=100s, M=5, L=15.

Baselines: the deployed in-app video-call assistants of Doubao (Seed 2.0) and Gemini (Gemini-3.1-flash-live), app versions from late May/early June 2026, driven through their apps with identical videos and questions posed at matched timestamps.
Protocol: 5 blinded LLM-researcher raters score quality and timing on a 3-level scale, equal-weight average per case, reported as win/tie/loss rates versus each baseline.

key_findings.finding: Making the response decision internal and per-second lets a compact 8B model beat far larger deployed turn-based video-call assistants in live, event-driven settings.
key_findings.evidence: Head-to-head blinded human evaluation over 58 cases: 77.6% wins / 17.2% ties / 5.2% losses against Doubao and 87.9% / 10.3% / 1.7% against Gemini, with the model winning more than it loses in every one of the six scenarios.

key_findings.finding: The advantage is largest precisely on the most timing-critical tasks, where turn-based or polling-based designs fail structurally.
key_findings.evidence: 100% win rate in monitoring and alerting against both baselines; 100% against Gemini and 80%/70% with zero losses against Doubao on real-time translation and counting. Case studies: alert issued at the instant of a fall versus Doubao's 4-5s lag (its polling interval) and Gemini's inability to monitor; all six dart throws counted on time versus two (delayed) and none; continuous subtitle translation versus baselines translating only the frame present when asked.

key_findings.finding: Baselines only close the gap where timing pressure is low, and then on answer quality rather than timing.
key_findings.evidence: Doubao's only foothold is live commentary (22.2% wins) driven by broader knowledge and richer phrasing, while its commentary timing is erratic (too frequent then too sparse) because its external trigger cannot judge when a remark is warranted; Gemini's only foothold is time awareness (10% wins, 40% ties) on ask-after-the-fact, user-triggered cases. JoyAI's own losses are confined to quality (occasional commentary hallucination).

key_findings.finding: Capabilities never present in training emerge from the shared per-second action format, suggesting a general watch-and-interact competence rather than scenario-specific tricks.
key_findings.evidence: With no app-interface video of any kind in training, the model guides a shopper through changing phone screens in step with each swipe; asked to narrate once every four seconds, it composes timed action with live commentary although the two never co-occur in training data; it also improvises a lecture from a slide deck and delegates HTML generation of an observed app screen to the background.

key_findings.finding: Designing the streaming memory around prefix reuse is what makes long-horizon, real-time serving deployable on off-the-shelf engines.
key_findings.evidence: Text-based mid/long-term tiers are prefilled once per chunk into a KV cache so only new frames and the previous reply are recomputed, and AdaCodec shrinks predictable frames to ~16 tokens; the system sustains over two hours of continuous video at sub-second end-to-end latency on standard vLLM, whereas sliding-window or token-pruning streaming methods break prefix reuse. Baseline products by contrast auto-hang-up (~5 min for Doubao, ~2m15s for Gemini), scoring nothing on roughly half the memory cases.
